items.gist: Defines occasional rites as arising from contingent circumstances, while fixed rites remain primary and pervade them.
Lists twenty-three kinds of occasional rites, including worship, initiations, festivals, and dream or command resolutions.
Introduces parvan days as twofold, kula and akula, with kula days enumerated first.
Explains kulaparva as the moment of full self-awareness arising through prana-based cakra movement and gathering.
Describes how yogini and siddha gatherings bring immediate fullness of consciousness and timely fruits.
Prescribes worship, tarpana, and siddhi practices on parvan days, while condemning negligent and impure conduct.
Classifies parvan days into six types according to general and special temporal conditions.
Enumerates lunar fortnights, nakshatras, tithis, times, and related parvan designations.
States that circle sacrifice should be performed especially on parvan days, with attention to its proper time.
Discusses the primacy of tithi and graha-nakshatra conjunction, with day and night divided into parts.
Argues that tithi, not mere time, is primary because it becomes manifest through graha and nakshatra.
Cites Bhairavakula and related texts on parvan worship, including special practices in certain months.
Gives results of circle worship and says tithi's natural arising should be observed when graha conjunction is absent.
Warns that neglecting parvan days is blameworthy, while omitting optional rites incurs no fault; cakrayaga is then set forth for anuyaga.
